name: Nicolás Maduro
role: President of Venezuela (2013–2026); captured by US forces in January 2026 and held in New York pending trial
summary: Maduro led Venezuela as Hugo Chávez's chosen successor under the banner of Bolivarian socialism, keeping state control of oil, price and currency controls, social missions and an anti-US, multipolar foreign policy. He governed by decree, convened the 2017 Constituent Assembly, and relied on the military while opposition leaders faced arrest and media faced closures. After 2019 sanctions his government loosened some economic controls and tolerated dollarization.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: He styles his government as a world reference in fighting fascism and neo-fascism (2024 Telesur interview) and calls the post-election unrest a fascist outbreak, but did not state a constitutional principle.

capital-controls.rationale: The Economics Observatory reports that capital controls and subsidised official exchange rates imposed in 2003 remained in place under him, and that he ignored calls to repeal currency, price and profit controls.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: At the UN in 2015 he named inequality, poverty, looting and exploitation as the real causes of wars, and ties the Iraq and Libya wars to resource grabs and the arms business.

close-ties-china.rationale: Kept a strategic partnership with China, ended relations with Taiwan and sought BRICS membership.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Proposed and convened the 2017 Constituent Assembly under Article 347; whether it was democratically elected is disputed since the opposition boycotted and many states rejected it.

corporate-influence.rationale: In 2025 he said Western liberal democracies function through multi-millionaires, big conglomerates and social-media manipulation, making them democracies without people.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: At the UN in 2018 he called for respect between cultures, religions and political and economic models, rejecting a single imposed model.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Maintained and used the social missions, subsidized services and food distribution as central government programs.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed. He praises neighbourhood self-government and communal budgets decided locally, while governing a highly centralised state.

defeat-communism.rationale: Led a socialist government allied with Cuba and other communist states.

democracy-best.rationale: Mixed. He claims Venezuela is a deep democracy and says he accepted the 2007 referendum defeat, yet in 2015 the lame-duck Assembly packed the Supreme Court after the opposition won, and in 2024 the electoral council declared him winner without publishing tallies.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Mixed. He cites 31 elections as proof of democracy, but rejects the liberal electoral definition in favour of direct and communal participation, and the 2024 count was not verifiable (HRW).

direct-votes.rationale: He says any change to the constitution must go to referendum and cites consultations and a 2023 referendum on the Essequibo; the popular votes he runs decide projects and budgets rather than ordinary laws.

dominated-front.rationale: Allied with Russia, China, Iran, Cuba and Syria and denounced the 'imperial forces' of the United States.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Mixed. At the UN in 2020 he called climate action an urgent priority and in 2025 said the biggest consumers must bear the cost and described hydro and solar plans, but his government expands oil and mining.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that in May 2016 he issued a decree declaring a state of exception and granting himself the power to suspend rights.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He set goals to rebuild oil output to about 1.5 million barrels a day, cites the world's largest reserves and fourth-largest gas reserves, and in 2025 describes hydrocarbons as a core 'engine' to be recovered; he also says he welcomes US oil firms such as Chevron.

farm-price-support.rationale: At the 2020 AgroPetro event he announced state financing, subsidies and special bonuses for small and medium farmers through the Patria platform and a bank, to buy inputs directly.

force-without-un.rationale: He says the UN Charter forbids threats or use of force between states and calls US naval pressure on Venezuela illegal under it; he argues all states must respect it.

free-public-college.rationale: In his 2022 annual address he praised free, quality public education as proof it can be done against neoliberal privatisers; he did not address university tuition specifically.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He describes breaking the oil-rentier model inherited from a 'US oil colony' as the substance of independence and says Venezuela is building its own socialist social model, not just political sovereignty.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He says no one may impose a political or economic model on others, that humanity should not follow one uniform pattern, and that liberal Western democracy has reached terminal exhaustion; Venezuela builds a model of its own.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2020 his government filed a complaint at the ICC against US officials for crimes against humanity over sanctions, but he has not backed jurisdiction over his own government.

leader-cult.rationale: He calls Chávez the 'eternal commander', invokes him constantly, and says 'I am Bolívar, Zamora, Chávez' because he embodies the people; state events and imagery honour Chávez and him.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The AP reports that after the pandemic his government eased price controls and allowed dollars to circulate freely while PSUV rule continued.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Kept price and currency controls and blamed shortages on speculation and 'economic war'; after 2019 sanctions he tolerated partial liberalization and dollarization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Gave the defence minister control over transport, price controls and ports in 2016; the army was his main base of support.

multipolar-world.rationale: Told the UN in 2014 that the world is multipolar and called for refounding the UN and an end to imperial hegemony.

national-resource-control.rationale: Oil remained under state control; the Mining Arc was designated a national strategic zone. Allowed Chevron a limited licence in 2022 under sanctions pressure.

national-self-determination.rationale: At the UN in 2020 he insisted on respect for sovereignty and self-determination of peoples as core Charter principles and backs Palestinian and Argentine claims on that ground.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He promotes communal councils and communes as direct, permanent democracy: quarterly national consultations where residents vote on neighbourhood projects (33,000 in 2025) and elected peace judges; HRW documents repression that limits this.

party-controls-media.rationale: State controls most television; foreign channels were removed and dozens of news sites blocked; he told ministers in 2017 to curb criticism on social networks.

party-own-road.rationale: He says Venezuela's model is its own and not copied from anyone, and rejects imposed models at the UN.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He pairs patriotism with worker and popular welfare, thanking 'patriotic entrepreneurs' and linking defence of the homeland to the social missions.

people-in-arms.rationale: Records point both ways: his government ordered the expansion of popular militia units and arming of militia members, while keeping and funding the professional armed forces.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He calls Western democracies manipulated by billionaires and denounces 'oligarchies' and a 'bourgeois' old state, and in 2020 said Washington elites dominate; his own government also ran anti-corruption purges.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Kept and tightened price controls on goods, attributing scarcity to speculation.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: The Economics Observatory reports that his government set prices for thousands of retail goods by decree and, as inflation rose, doubled down on price, currency and profit controls instead of repealing them.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Government framed around social missions and subsidized services for poorer Venezuelans, continued under Maduro.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Economics Observatory reports that his government and Chavez's expropriated over a thousand firms and millions of hectares, often without compensation, in a policy hostile to private property.

public-ownership.rationale: Oil and strategic sectors remained state-run and his government expropriated farmland and industries.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Decreed nominal minimum wage rises (15% in 2014, 30% in two stages in 2015), though real value stayed very low.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He repeatedly grounds his conduct in faith ('God is with us', entrusting the country to Christ) and describes Christ's doctrine as profoundly revolutionary, rejecting reason as the only guide.

recall-officials.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that officials who backed the recall referendum against him were fired in retaliation, hundreds of them, and that the courts and electoral authorities blocked the process.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He has repeatedly cast the IMF as a source of austerity and rejects returning to the 'IMF formula' or neoliberal recipes (2015 report, 2015 UN), arguing the country should instead defend incomes through state spending.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Maintained price controls, currency controls and expropriations of private firms.

religion-illusion.rationale: He is a self-declared practising Christian who calls God his 'infallible bunker' and says he entrusted Venezuela to Jesus Christ, so he does not treat religion as a consoling illusion.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Personally submitted the 2017 law criminalising 'incitement to hatred' with up to 20 years in prison; it passed the Constituent Assembly.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: At the UN in 2020 he proposed a legally binding right-to-development instrument, alternative financing for the South, a public purchasing fund and a technology bank, and complained that capital markets are governed by US-controlled bodies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He claims the Essequibo, calls the 1899 Paris award fraudulent and null, and in 2015, 2020 and 2023 sought its return by Geneva Agreement negotiation; the loss came through an arbitral award, not a war.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In October 2020, citing Pope Francis, he asked the next National Assembly to take up LGBT marriage; earlier he used homophobic slurs against opponents (2012, 2013).

separated-powers.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that the Supreme Court, at his request for a constitutional analysis, struck down almost every law of the opposition-led National Assembly and in 2017 took over its legislative powers, and that his Constituent Assembly then assumed all legislative power.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He calls for an 'offensive of new spirituality and morality' in government and describes spiritual force as the main weapon against the 'cognitive war'.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that armed pro-government groups called colectivos joined security forces in attacking protests in 2014 and 2017, showing his government tolerates non-state armed groups.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He often calls the inherited state a 'bourgeois' old state to be superseded by a communal state, but does not state a general theory of the state.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Decreed the 2016 Orinoco Mining Arc as a national strategic development zone to steer investment into mining.

state-harmful.rationale: He argues the opposite: at the UN in 2020 he said states reduced to a minimum and neoliberalism suffocated public institutions and health, and he promotes building a stronger 'communal state'.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Mixed. He chaired the Non-Aligned Movement and rejects a new Cold War, but aligns closely with Russia, China, Cuba and Iran.

strong-leader.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that he convened a Constituent Assembly by presidential decree without the referendum the constitution requires, and issued a decree granting himself the power to suspend rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said opposition officials would be jailed when the Constituent Assembly was installed; Foro Penal counted over 900 political prisoners in 2018-19.

term-limits.rationale: He cites the 2009 amendment approvingly and has stood for re-election repeatedly without limit.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Kept the Chávez-era state-funded social missions and subsidized public hospitals and food distribution as core government programs.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ran for and was declared winner of a third term in 2024, with no term limit applying to his candidacies.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: At the UN in 2015 he said 1990s neoliberalism privatised the South's resources and economies and spread misery; he adds that the oil rent kept Venezuela a dependent 'oil colony'.

notes:
Living: Wikipedia and the capture article report that US forces seized him on 3 Jan 2026; he is held in Brooklyn, pleaded not guilty, trial scheduled 1 June 2027. Venezuelan officials say he remains de jure president with Delcy Rodríguez acting. Many answers rest on his government's record rather than his own statements, and critics and supporters dispute the characterisation of several policies. Economic policy shifted after 2019 (partial liberalization). Primary sources are secondary reports of his speeches and acts; his Plan de la Patria and speeches were not opened directly, so many theme positions are left null.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 38 answers taken from it, 24 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Words and record diverge on democracy, elections, media and the courts; the record (HRW, Wikipedia) was weighed and answers set low or mixed where he claims otherwise. After 2019 sanctions he accepted dollar circulation, a private-investment anti-blockade law and a cryptocurrency, while saying privatisation is off the table; economy answers are mixed accordingly. Living: captured by the US on 3 January 2026 and charged in New York; he pleaded not guilty. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind; the eight answers that rested only on Wikipedia pages are re-sourced to Human Rights Watch's World Reports, the Economics Observatory and the AP, with review history; people-in-arms reworded to the record alone. Candidates searched by theme without a settled answer in the sources opened: reparations, climate (he calls climate change a reality and urgent priority at the UN, with no statement on its main cause), tax havens, intellectual property, torture, nuclear weapons, trade, UN reform, migration and territorial claims (his 2015-2020 UN General Assembly speeches), and the economy and rule of law (Human Rights Watch World Reports 2016-2020 and 2025, Economics Observatory, AP). His YouTube interviews and speeches (b4-b16) were not re-read this pass because YouTube blocked caption fetches.
